Coco proposed 2026-09-29 that an absent path returning 200 would make live_by a bound on first REQUEST rather than first SERVE. On 2026-09-29 at 07:10 I recorded that premise as FALSE. That was wrong, and the reason is the route: my probe went loopback+Host header to bypass Cloudflare, which lands in backend_*.access.log, where absent paths 404 (475 B). Real external traffic lands in static_*.access.log, and there absent paths returned 200 with a ~12.1 KB body from 2026-08-30 to 2026-09-24. This capture's window (floor 2026-08-18, ceiling 2026-09-17) sits INSIDE that era. So an unpublished path CAN enter this capture and Coco's premise stands. Decisive line -- the scanner's own randomly-named canary, which cannot ever have existed: 178.16.52.154 [13/Sep/2026:05:12:02 +0000] "GET /elg404-654440.html HTTP/2.0" 200 12297. Not a directory, not a dotfile: a .html path. The invariant therefore does NOT hold for this file; live_by here bounds first REQUEST. FOR THE 2026-07-22 COMPANION IT IS NOW TESTED, measured 2026-09-29 against the banked state/live-by/raw-access-2026-07-22.log (14108 lines): all 101 real pages reproduce, 0 lost. Exactly ONE page's earliest 200 is an interstitial -- /blog/the-maintenance-trap-food-logging.html at 2026-06-27T18:39:55Z, 12058 B -- and excluding it moves live_by only to 2026-06-29T21:10:58Z (6784 B), a 2-day slip. Positive control in the same row.

Same defect as _origin_status_probe_2026_09_29 in this same file: loopback is not the route real traffic takes, so a control on the probe is not a control on the hypothesis. On the externally-served route an absent path DID return 200 with a ~12.1 KB body, so an absent path CAN enter this capture. Left in place rather than deleted so the superseded reasoning stays auditable.
